correctness.rationale: Phi has no disk zeros. Its logarithmic derivative is 1+U(-w), U=sec+tan with strictly positive coefficients from U'=(1+U²)/2. The sharp pointwise bound is achieved at w=-s. Higher-order Schwarz factorization omega=z^m eta and Schwarz--Pick yield the exact radial expression, with an explicit real Blaschke eta attaining all inequalities. Direct Schwarz--Pick gives G(s)=(1-s²)(1+U(s)). Monotonicity of the critical ratio gives a unique maximizer. Boundary Blaschke concentration proves the same sharp norm for all finite m; the equality case of Schwarz--Pick forbids interior saturation for m>=2. Exact rational checker brackets r*; the infinite theorem is analytic.

value.rationale: The pre-Schwarzian norm is a natural quantitative local-distortion invariant. Prescribing the initial Taylor-jet gap is a standard mathematical normalization. The exact radial envelope and all finite-order extremizer constructions establish the precise effect of this normalization on pointwise distortion; the common sharp global constant and boundary-concentration mechanism show that arbitrary finite flatness at the origin cannot improve the class norm. The claim is not just a trivial identity or numerical estimate and makes no assertion for globally univalent subfamilies.
